name: Buddha Maya Gardens
summary: A garden hotel run by the Kathmandu Guest House group, set in quiet grounds about a five-minute walk from the Sacred Garden. It has been hosting pilgrims and tour groups for around 25 years and is our first choice for most Lumbini stays.
body: Buddha Maya Gardens sits just outside the Sacred Garden on the southern side of the Lumbini master-plan area, close enough to walk to the Maya Devi Temple at opening time. The hotel belongs to the KGH Group, which also runs the long-established Kathmandu Guest House, and it has operated in Lumbini for about a quarter of a century. Low buildings spread around lawns and trees, so the atmosphere is calm even when groups are in residence.

Rooms are comfortable rather than lavish, with the standard comforts of a good Nepali 3-star hotel. The in-house restaurant serves Nepali, Indian and continental dishes, and vegetarian meals are easy to arrange for pilgrim groups. Staff are used to helping with bicycle hire, monastery visits and early starts for the Sacred Garden. The hotel also hosts wellness and meditation stays, which suits guests on our retreat package.
why: About five minutes' walk to the Sacred Garden and Maya Devi Temple
Quiet garden setting, well suited to early-rising pilgrims
Experienced with groups, vegetarian meals and meditation stays

faqs.q: How far is Buddha Maya Gardens from the Maya Devi Temple?
faqs.a: It is about a five-minute walk from the Sacred Garden entrance, which makes it one of the closest comfortable hotels to the Maya Devi Temple. Guests can easily reach the temple at opening time for morning chanting, return for breakfast, and go out again by bicycle for the monasteries.

faqs.q: Does Buddha Maya Gardens serve vegetarian food?
faqs.a: Yes. The restaurant serves Nepali, Indian and continental dishes with plenty of vegetarian choices, and the kitchen is used to pilgrim groups. Jain or no-onion-no-garlic meals can usually be prepared with advance notice; we pass on dietary requests when booking.

faqs.q: Is Buddha Maya Gardens good for families?
faqs.a: Yes. The garden grounds give children space to play, the location keeps travel to the Sacred Garden short, and staff can arrange bicycles and rickshaws for the monastic zone. Family and connecting room availability varies, so tell us your group size early, especially for April and May.

name: Lumbini Hokke Hotel
summary: A Japanese-style hotel in the Lumbini area with tatami rooms, shoji screens and a courtyard layout, long popular with Japanese and other East Asian pilgrims. It offers a quiet, distinctive stay close to the monasteries and the Sacred Garden.
body: Lumbini Hokke Hotel was built to serve Japanese pilgrims and still feels distinctly Japanese, with a choice of tatami-floored rooms behind paper shoji screens alongside Western-style rooms. The buildings are arranged around a courtyard garden, which keeps the hotel calm. It lies within easy reach of the World Peace Pagoda, the monastic zone and the Sacred Garden by car, rickshaw or bicycle.

The hotel is not new, and some guests note that rooms show their age, but service is attentive and the breakfast spread is often praised. Japanese dishes appear on the menu alongside Nepali and continental food. Staff help with taxis, luggage storage and currency exchange. It suits travellers who value a quiet, characterful stay over modern design, and Buddhist groups from East Asia in particular.
why: Japanese-style tatami rooms, rare in Nepal
Calm courtyard layout near the monasteries and Peace Pagoda
Well regarded for service and breakfast

faqs.q: Does Lumbini Hokke Hotel have Japanese-style rooms?
faqs.a: Yes. The hotel offers traditional Japanese-style rooms with tatami floors and shoji screens, as well as Western-style rooms with beds. Japanese rooms have futon bedding on the floor, so seniors who find low beds difficult should request a Western room when booking.

faqs.q: Is Lumbini Hokke Hotel close to the Maya Devi Temple?
faqs.a: It is within the wider Lumbini area, a short drive, rickshaw ride or cycle from the Sacred Garden and close to the monastic zone and World Peace Pagoda. It is not quite as close to the Maya Devi Temple as hotels right beside the Sacred Garden, but transfers take only a few minutes.

No, it is an older property, and some rooms show wear, such as marked paper screens. Guests usually choose it for its Japanese character, calm courtyard, service and breakfast rather than modern fittings. If up-to-date rooms matter most, we suggest Buddha Maya Gardens instead.

name: Hotel Nirvana
summary: A long-established hotel on Paklihawa Road in Bhairahawa (Siddharthanagar), with a garden, restaurant and bar, about 20 km from Lumbini. It is the practical choice for late flights, early border crossings and groups covering Ramagrama and Devdaha.
body: Hotel Nirvana sits on Paklihawa Road in central Bhairahawa, a short drive from Gautam Buddha International Airport and about 15 minutes from the Belahiya border post. It has been one of the town's main hotels for many years, used by tour groups, business travellers and families crossing from India. Rooms are spacious and standard for a good Nepali business hotel, with a garden giving some quiet away from the town's traffic.

The restaurant and bar serve Nepali, Indian, Chinese and continental food, and breakfast starts early, which helps on border and flight days. Recent guests have mentioned updates to the facilities. From here Lumbini is 30–40 minutes by car, Ramagrama about 1.25 hours and Devdaha about 45 minutes, so the hotel works well as a base for the eastern Buddhist sites or a first night after crossing from India.
why: Close to the airport and about 15 minutes from the Sonauli–Belahiya border
Garden, restaurant and bar in a central location
Good base for Ramagrama, Devdaha and onward drives

faqs.q: How far is Hotel Nirvana from the Sonauli border?
faqs.a: Hotel Nirvana is in central Bhairahawa, about 4–5 km from the Belahiya border post, roughly 15 minutes by car or rickshaw. It is a convenient first or last night for travellers crossing between India and Nepal, especially if you arrive late in the day.

faqs.q: Should I stay at Hotel Nirvana or in Lumbini?
faqs.a: Choose Hotel Nirvana if you arrive late by air or road, cross the border early, or plan to visit Ramagrama and Devdaha. Choose Lumbini if your focus is the Maya Devi Temple and monasteries, since staying there lets you walk to the Sacred Garden at dawn.

faqs.q: Is Hotel Nirvana close to the airport?
faqs.a: Yes. Gautam Buddha International Airport is on the western edge of Bhairahawa, a short drive from the hotel. It is a sensible choice before an early flight to Kathmandu or after an evening arrival, and we include airport transfers in our packages.

name: Hotel Srinagar
summary: Tansen's long-running 3-star hotel, set on the Srinagar hill road about 1.2 km above the old town, with gardens, a children's play area and mountain views on clear days. Operating for around five decades, it is the most comfortable base in Palpa.
body: Hotel Srinagar was among the first 3-star hotels in Nepal's western hills and has been running for around five decades. It stands on the link road climbing from Tansen towards Srinagar hill, about 1.2 km from the town centre, which means fresher air and quieter nights than in the old town, and an easy start for the sunrise walk to the Srinagar viewpoint. On clear mornings from October to March, the Himalaya is visible from the grounds.

Facilities are traditional rather than modern: a restaurant, garden terraces, parking, and a playground that families appreciate. Recent reviews are mixed on room condition relative to price, so expect a dependable, older hill hotel rather than a boutique stay. We use it because it is the best-located comfortable option in Tansen, and staff are used to arranging Rani Mahal trips and old-town guides.
why: Quiet hillside location close to the Srinagar sunrise viewpoint
Gardens and mountain views on clear days
Long experience hosting tour groups in Palpa

faqs.q: How far is Hotel Srinagar from Tansen town?
faqs.a: About 1.2 km uphill on the Srinagar link road, roughly 15–20 minutes' walk down to the old town or five minutes by car. Walking back up is a steady climb. Our drivers provide transfers for the evening walk and dinner in town if needed.

faqs.q: Can you see mountains from Hotel Srinagar?
faqs.a: Yes, on clear days, mostly from October to March in the early morning. Dhaulagiri and the Annapurna range can appear above the ridges to the north. For the fullest panorama, walk 30–45 minutes up to the Srinagar hill viewpoint at sunrise.

faqs.q: Is Hotel Srinagar a modern hotel?
faqs.a: No, it is an older property that has operated for around five decades, and reviews note that some rooms are dated. It remains the most comfortable well-located choice in Tansen, with gardens, views and helpful staff. Set expectations for a traditional hill hotel rather than a new resort.
